overview.overview:
Kansas is forecast to vote Republican in 2028, with an expected margin of about 10 points. The state backed the Republican presidential nominee in 2020 by about 14.6 points and in 2024 by about 16.1 points. The plausible range runs from a Republican win of roughly 1 point to one of about 19 points, so a Republican victory is the central expectation across that band.

No public polls or state-specific headlines are available for the contest, so the outlook rests on the state's voting history and the broader national environment. With six electoral votes and a result well to the right of the national margin, Kansas is unlikely to be decisive in the Electoral College.
overview.watch: A large, sustained shift in national opinion toward Democrats, far beyond current expectations, would be needed to narrow the gap here meaningfully.
key_factors: Kansas voted Republican in 2020 and 2024 by margins above 14 points.
The state leans roughly 16 points more Republican than the nation, and the expected margin favors Republicans by about 10 points.
No public polling or candidate-specific information is currently available for the state.
